dataset_info.name: VEDA AyurMind AI — Diseases & Therapeutic Herbs Dataset
dataset_info.part_description: Diseases DIS-001 to DIS-060 (A to F)
dataset_info.source_text: Dravyaguna Vijnana — Therapeutic Indication of Drugs & Technical Medical Terminology
dataset_info.description: Part 1 of 3 — Ayurvedic disease-herb mapping. Each entry includes disease ID, English name, Sanskrit name, category, description, herbs with botanical names, associated Sanskrit technical terms with meanings, and herb count.

fields_explained.english_name: Standard English name of the disease/condition
fields_explained.herbs: List of Ayurvedic herbs — name + botanical for cross-reference
fields_explained.associated_sanskrit_terms: All Sanskrit technical terms directly related to this disease with English meanings

diseases.description: Substances or conditions that induce termination of pregnancy. Used in classical Ayurveda under specific therapeutic indications.
Localised collection of pus in body tissue; painful swelling with redness, heat and inflammation. Caused by bacterial infection and Pitta aggravation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Diminished digestive fire (Agni); impaired gastric function leading to sluggish digestion, bloating and accumulation of Ama (metabolic toxins). Equivalent to modern dyspepsia.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Food intoxication associated with faulty digestion and impaired metabolism
Stimulating the factor of gastro-intestinal digestion

diseases.description: Chronic excessive alcohol consumption causing physical and mental derangement; liver damage, cognitive impairment and bodily toxicity.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Alcoholism; effect of excessive use of alcohol
Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Loss of hair from scalp or body; patchy or complete baldness. In Ayurveda related to Pitta aggravation, Vata vitiation and weak Rakta dhatu.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: Painful joint condition caused by accumulation of Ama (undigested metabolic toxins) in joints with Vata vitiation. Closely correlates with rheumatoid arthritis — features joint swelling, pain, stiffness, and systemic inflammation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Food intoxication associated with faulty digestion and impaired metabolism
Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Characterised by hyperacidity, burning sensation in stomach and throat, abdominal pain, biliary nausea, sour eructations and abnormal gastric feeling. Equivalent to GERD and peptic conditions.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Acid gastritis; hyperacidity with burning sensation, abdominal pain and biliary nausea

diseases.description: Deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin causing pallor, fatigue, weakness and breathlessness. In Ayurveda linked to impaired Rakta dhatu (blood tissue) formation and Pitta vitiation.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Anti-anaemic; indicated in treatment of anaemia
Nourishing and promoting body tissues; nutrient tissue homologues

diseases.description: Loss of appetite; lack of desire to eat food; often accompanied by tastelessness and aversion to food. Related to Agnimandya in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Tastelessness of mouth; tasteless state of oral cavity

diseases.description: Tuberculous infection of cervical lymph nodes causing swelling and enlargement of neck glands. Chronic lymphadenopathy of the neck.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Cervical adenitis; chain of swollen glands in neck
Glandular enlargement, swelling and other symptoms
Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Substances promoting sexual vigour, potency, libido and reproductive health. Vajikara herbs nourish Shukra dhatu (reproductive tissue) and enhance virility.
Inflammation of joints with pain, stiffness and reduced mobility. In Ayurveda primarily a Vata disorder involving joint spaces.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disease caused by vitiation of Vata and Rakta; gout
Group of diseases caused by aggravated Vata — pain, convulsion, paralysis
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Chronic respiratory condition with recurrent breathlessness, wheezing and chest tightness due to airway inflammation and mucus accumulation. Classified as Kapha-Vata disorder in Ayurveda.
Pathological condition of excessively strong digestive fire causing rapid burning of food and body tissues (dhatus), leading to severe hunger, emaciation and debility.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive hunger and digestion causing loss of dhatus, emaciation and debility

diseases.description: Painful pus-filled skin infections (furuncles) caused by bacterial infection of hair follicles. Represents Pitta-Rakta vitiation in Ayurveda.
Tissue injury caused by heat, fire, chemicals or radiation; causes local destruction, pain and scarring.
Generalised or localised burning sensation in the body; often linked to Pitta aggravation, heat disorders or inflammatory states.

Hard mineral deposits forming in kidneys or urinary tract causing severe colicky pain, haematuria and urinary obstruction. Mutra-ashmari relates to urinary stones; Pitta-ashmari to gall bladder stones.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Calculus; stone — Mutra-ashmari (urinary) and Pitta-ashmari (gall bladder)

diseases.description: Small sand-like micro-calculi in the urine causing irritation, painful urination and gritty sensation during voiding.
Pain or discomfort in the chest region; may relate to cardiac, pulmonary, musculoskeletal or digestive causes. Includes Parsvashula (side/chest pain).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Colic pain occurring in the iliac or pelvic region of the abdomen; chest pain

diseases.description: Severe spasmodic abdominal pain caused by intestinal gas, obstruction, muscle spasm or Vata accumulation in digestive tract.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Colic; ache; pain; disease or symptom
Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements; hard, dry stools; straining during defecation. Caused by Vata aggravation in the colon (Purishavaha Srotas).
Wasting disease of the lungs; pulmonary tuberculosis with chronic cough, fever, haemoptysis, night sweats and progressive weight loss. The 'king of diseases' in Ayurveda.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Wasting condition of body due to chest-wound
Promoting body strength; muscular strength; resistance to diseases; tonic

diseases.description: Substances or preparations used to prevent conception. Classical Ayurvedic contraceptive herbs affect uterine receptivity or sperm viability.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Measures prescribed for reversal of sex in foetus during pregnancy

diseases.description: Acute inflammation of nasal mucosa with running nose, sneezing, nasal congestion, and mild fever. Caused by Kapha and Vata vitiation in the nasal passages.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated in treatment of chronic rhinitis
Curing and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: Forceful expulsion of air from lungs; dry or productive; acute or chronic. Classified into Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Ksataja (traumatic) and Kshayaja (consumptive) types in Ayurveda.
Abnormal growth of tissue; cystic or tumorous mass. Arbuda in Ayurveda refers to both benign and malignant growths arising from Tridosha imbalance.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Abdominal lump caused by accumulation of wind and other causes

diseases.description: Frequent loose or watery stools; acute or chronic; associated with fluid and electrolyte loss. Classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Bhayaja (fear-induced), Shokaja (grief-induced) and Sannipataja types.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorders of intestinal tract; malabsorption syndrome; amoebiasis/colitis

diseases.description: Diarrhoea with blood in stools; dysentery with bleeding; indicates intestinal mucosal damage and Pitta-Rakta vitiation.
Various disorders of the oral cavity including stomatitis, ulcers, infections and inflammation of gums, tongue and buccal mucosa.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated or useful to cleanse the mouth
Inflamed gums with haemorrhage and foul smell

diseases.description: Inflammation of the mucous membrane lining the mouth; mouth sores, ulcers (aphthous ulcers) and pain on eating.
Various disorders affecting teeth and supporting structures including caries, loose teeth, toothache, gum disease and dental sensitivity.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dentrifice; promoting teeth/dental health; curing dental ailments
Inflamed gums with haemorrhage and foul smell

diseases.description: Various disorders of the throat including tonsillitis, pharyngitis, laryngitis and diphtheria.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Diphtheria; infectious disease of throat and air passage
Curing, cleaning and improving throat disorders; soothing to throat

diseases.description: Absence of menstrual periods in women of reproductive age; primary (never started) or secondary (previously regular but stopped).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive discharge of menstrual blood; menorrhagia

diseases.description: Abnormal white or yellowish vaginal discharge; may indicate infection, hormonal imbalance or uterine pathology. Related to Kapha vitiation.
Abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding. Classified as Pitta-Rakta vitiation causing excessive flow from Artavavaha Srotas.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive discharge of menstrual blood; menorrhagia
Intrinsic haemorrhage due to vitiation of rakta and pitta
A lump formed in uterus due to accumulation of menstrual blood

diseases.description: Inability to conceive after regular unprotected intercourse; male or female reproductive failure. Related to deficient Shukra dhatu or Artava.
Intestinal inflammation causing severe diarrhoea with blood and mucus, abdominal cramps and tenesmus (painful urge to defecate). Corresponds to amoebiasis and bacillary dysentery.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorders of intestinal tract; malabsorption syndrome

diseases.description: Painful, difficult or burning sensation during urination; may accompany UTI, urinary stones or prostatic conditions.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Dysuria associated with burning sensation, yellow urine or haematuria

diseases.description: Various disorders of the ear including otitis media, otitis externa, ear infections and discharge. Encompasses earache, deafness and tinnitus.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Earache; symptom or type of ear disorders
Otorrhoea; bleeding; pus formation in ear
Tinnitus; a kind of ear disease
Swelling with itching in ear pinnae

diseases.description: Partial or complete loss of hearing; may be conductive or sensorineural. In Ayurveda often caused by Vata aggravation in the ear channel.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Anti-vata; indicated in diseases of nervous system

diseases.description: Pain in the ear; may result from infection, inflammation, referred pain from teeth or jaw, or Vata vitiation in ear channels.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Earache; symptom or type of ear disorders

diseases.description: Discharge of pus or fluid from the ear; indicates active infection or perforated eardrum.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Otorrhoea; bleeding and pus formation in the ear

diseases.description: Excessive thinness, wasting of body mass and muscular atrophy. Caused by deficient nutrition, chronic illness or depleted Ojas (vital energy).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Emaciation; promoting slimming of the body
Promoting body strength; muscular strength; tonic
Aids in reducing corpulence — opposing action

diseases.description: Recurrent seizures from abnormal electrical brain activity; loss of consciousness, convulsions and post-ictal confusion. Classified as Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja and Sannipataja.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A vatic disorder with fits of convulsions and loss of consciousness

diseases.description: Acute streptococcal skin infection with spreading red, swollen, warm and painful skin patches often with fever. In Ayurveda a Pitta-dominant spreading condition.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Type of erysipelas causing glandular inflammation with high fever
Syndrome like erysipelas causing fever and swelling
Syndrome causing skin inflammation with burning, redness and intense pain

diseases.description: Various disorders affecting the eyes including infections, inflammation, conjunctivitis, glaucoma, cataracts and visual defects. A major category in Ayurvedic Shalakya Tantra (ENT & ophthalmology).

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Diseases of the eye; ophthalmic diseases
Beneficial to structure, function and prevention of eye ailments
Pterygium; a kind of eye disease
Staphyloma; a kind of eye disease
Chronic eye disease resulting in watering, itching and blurred vision

diseases.description: Inflammation of the conjunctiva causing redness, discharge, watering and irritation of the eye. Includes infective and allergic types.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Conjunctivitis; a kind of eye disease
Ophthalmia neonatorum; inflammation of eye in new-born child

diseases.description: Inability to see well in dim light or darkness; often linked to Vitamin A deficiency and depleted Rasa and Rakta dhatu affecting the eyes.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Beneficial to structure, function and prevention of eye ailments

diseases.description: Transient loss of consciousness (syncope) from cardiac, neurological or metabolic causes. In Ayurveda caused by diminished Ojas and Pitta accumulation in Hridaya (heart).

Elevated body temperature above normal as the body's immune response to infection or inflammation. The most common disease in Ayurveda; classified into many types including Vataja, Pittaja, Kaphaja, Sannipataja and exogenous (agantuja) fevers.
Persistent or recurring fever lasting more than two weeks; associated with debility, depleted Ojas and chronic infections or inflammatory states.

Intermittent fever caused by Plasmodium parasite transmitted by mosquito; periodic chills, rigors, high temperature and profuse sweating. Corresponds to Caturthika (quartan) and other periodic fevers.
Parasitic disease caused by filarial worms causing lymphatic obstruction, progressive limb swelling and elephantiasis. Lymphoedema from worm invasion of lymphatic vessels.
Abnormal tunnel connecting the anal canal to surrounding skin; usually follows anorectal abscess and causes chronic infection and discharge.
Accumulation of gas in digestive tract causing abdominal distension, discomfort, rumbling and belching. Classic Vata disorder in the digestive system.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorder with excessive gas in stomach; vitiation of Vata
Stages of Adhmana; hardness in abdomen caused by wind in bowels

diseases.description: Break or crack in a bone from trauma, stress or pathological weakening. Ayurvedic treatment focuses on bone union and Asthi dhatu (bone tissue) regeneration.
Substances that promote or increase breast milk production in nursing mothers. Vital postpartum therapeutic in Ayurveda.
Substances that purify or improve the quality of breast milk. Important in Ayurvedic paediatric care (Kaumarabhritya).
Abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland presenting as visible swelling at base of neck; may be diffuse or nodular. Related to Kapha and Vata vitiation causing glandular swelling.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Cervical adenitis; chain of swollen glands in neck
Glandular enlargement, swelling and other symptoms
